**Chinese name:** 兆易创新科技集团股份有限公司 (Zhàoyì Chuàngxīn Kējì Jítuán Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Founded 2005; one of the largest NOR flash and MCU suppliers globally, representing the mass-market, lower-complexity end of China's fabless sector rather than the leading-edge/AI segment most export-control coverage focuses on. It has gone dual-listed (H shares on HKEX since 13 January 2026, 03986.HK, ~HK$4.61bn net) and is a listed proxy on China's memory champion: it holds ~1.80% of CXMT/长鑫科技, which IPO'd on the STAR Market on 27 July 2026 in the largest STAR listing ever (¥57.92 billion raised, day-one market cap >¥3 trillion) — though, per the interim report, that stake is carried as 其他权益工具投资, so its revaluation flows to equity, not to P&L. The 2026 global memory supply crunch (AI-driven DRAM/NAND demand tightening prices across the board) lifted GigaDevice's pricing power sharply: H1 2026 revenue of ¥11.57 billion (+178.7% YoY) and net profit of ¥6.86 billion (+1,091.5% YoY, incl. ¥2.23bn fair-value gains on listed securities other than CXMT), per the interim report of 18 August 2026. Management's 1 September briefing guided H2 DRAM up 'moderately', expects 2027 tightness not to ease, and SLC NAND strength to run at least through 2027; the CXMT foundry-related procurement cap was raised again on 29 September to ¥7.85 billion for 2026 (¥4.41 billion pre-estimated for Jan–Apr 2027).
:::

## What does this firm design?

NOR flash memory chips, general-purpose microcontrollers, and sensors for consumer electronics, industrial, and automotive applications.
